raw_response:
**My reasoning:**

I've been working this land since I was in my twenties. In Quzhou, everyone around me grows winter wheat and summer maize — it's been that way my whole life, and for good reason. The soil is flat loam, the county has irrigation wells, and the market for both crops is reliable. I can sell to the local grain station or hold and wait for prices. I'm not trying anything new at 55. My kids have moved to the city, so it's mostly me and my wife. We have about 10 mu.

For wheat, I'll sow in mid-October after rotary-tilling the maize stubble under. I'll use良星44 seed — the county agricultural office pushed it a few years back and my neighbor gets good results. I put down base fertilizer when I sow, then top-dress urea at jointing in spring. I irrigate three times: once after sowing if the ground is dry, once at jointing, once at heading. My son told me to cut irrigations but I'm not risking it — water is still cheap enough from the well. Two pesticide passes: herbicide in winter, then an aphid and white powder mold spray in May.

After wheat harvest in early June, I'll directly seed summer maize the same day or the next — no time to waste, the growing season is short. I use郑单958, it's reliable. Maize mostly gets by on summer rain but I'll run one irrigation if July is dry at seedling stage. One herbicide pass after emergence. I'll harvest in late September.
